We needed .docx/.xlsx drag-and-drop on a self-hosted `opencode web` (1.18.25 → 1.18.29, Linux arm64) and ended up instrumenting the same code paths as @revaza88. A few findings not in this thread yet, in case they save someone time:

1. `attachmentMime()` has two rejections, not one. After the NUL-byte check there is a control-character ratio check (`> 0.3` of the first 4096 bytes). OOXML zips are ~0.13 so they only hit the NUL check, but legacy OLE2 files (.doc/.xls/.ppt, ~0.49) are rejected by the ratio check as well. Extending the accept list alone won't let those through.

2. Once a binary passes the client gate it is labeled `text/plain` and sent as a `data:` URL. On the server, `resolvePart` turns `text/plain` data parts into synthetic `Called the Read tool …` + raw-content text parts *before* `chat.message` plugin hooks run. So a client-only fix leaks the raw bytes into the prompt as text — we saw the zip bytes land in context even though our hook had already replaced the file part.

3. What worked for us end-to-end (web drop, paste, and `run --file`): disable the two client checks (we patched the embedded bundle; upstream this could be the `attachment.types`-style allowlist suggested above) plus a server-side `chat.message` plugin that ignores the declared mime, sniffs magic bytes (`PK\x03\x04` with `word/` | `xl/` | `ppt/` entries, the OLE2 header, `%PDF-`), converts documents to text (pandoc / LibreOffice / pandas in our setup), and replaces non-document binaries with a visible notice so they never reach the model as text. Verified with a headless-Chromium drop test against the real bundle for docx/xlsx/pptx/doc, mixed drops, and a random-binary guard. The remaining wart is the duplicated synthetic part from (2), which a plugin cannot prevent.

4. Trap: over a remote plain-HTTP origin nothing attaches at all, regardless of this fix — that is #41706 / #47645 (`crypto.subtle` unavailable in insecure contexts). Test over HTTPS or `localhost`.

If maintainers prefer the server-side direction, the smallest upstream change that makes this cleanly pluggable is running the `text/plain` synthetic-part injection after plugin hooks (or letting hooks see the raw file part first), plus the allowlist. Happy to share the hook if useful.

Reproduced on v1.18.29 (Linux arm64, `opencode web` bound to a Tailscale IP, opened from another machine as `http://<magicdns-name>:4096`). Same symptom: drop / paste / attach button all silently discard the file, no toast. Console: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'digest')` at `putBlob` → `blobID` (`packages/app/src/utils/draft-store.ts`).

One detail that may explain why this keeps being re-reported: the fix merged for #41706 — #42706 (2026-08-15) — went into the `v2` branch, not `dev`. `dev` and the v1.18.x tags still call `crypto.subtle.digest` unconditionally (`draft-store.ts:25`, and `blobReference` in `packages/session-ui/src/v2/components/prompt-input/attachments.ts:225` for the V2 composer), so 1.18.27 / 1.18.29 still fail. The PRs open against `dev` (#41710, #44735, #45263, #46418) are the ones that would actually reach a release.

Workaround that worked for us without touching the client: make the origin a secure context. `tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://<bind-ip>:4096` gives an `https://<name>.ts.net` URL (requires "Enable HTTPS" in the tailnet DNS settings). On that origin `isSecureContext` is true and attachments work end-to-end — verified with a headless-Chromium drop test against the real bundle; `opencode run --attach https://…` works through it as well. `http://localhost` works too, as noted above.

I hit the same failure mode with GLM 5.3 in the normal build agent: the model brainstormed and hallucinated instead of executing, then returned a normal stop before the requested work was complete. I had to send `continue` three times; on the fourth prompt I explicitly told it to stop brainstorming, update the todos quickly, and execute the work.

This suggests two useful acceptance criteria beyond an opt-in infinite mode:

- The default build flow should make execution-first behavior explicit: do not restart planning or brainstorming when actionable todos remain; inspect the current todos and execute the next unfinished item.
- A normal provider `stop` should not be treated as task completion when the session has unfinished todos, unless the user explicitly asked for a response-only turn.

Automatic continuation still needs strict bounds and must stop for pending permissions/questions, provider errors, interruptions, or repeated no-progress turns. The current behavior makes users manually type `continue` even when the session state already shows unfinished work.

Still reproducible on `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-19242` on macOS arm64.

Running `opencode2` repeatedly tried to start the background server, then returned:

```text
Starting background server...
Error: Timed out waiting for the background service to start
```

The log at `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` and running `opencode2 serve --service --print-
logs --log-level debug` exposed the underlying error:

```text
Managed service port 49374 on 127.0.0.1 is already in use by another process.
```

`lsof -nP -iTCP:49374` showed nothing, but `netstat -anv -p tcp | rg 49374` showed macOS’s
`symptomsd` listening on `*.49374`. A separate socket bind test confirmed “Address already in use.”

Switching to a free port restored startup:

```sh
opencode2 service set port 49375
opencode2 service start
```

Confirmed the service was listening on `127.0.0.1:49375`. The remaining problem is that the CLI still
hides the actionable port-conflict error behind a generic timeout.

Were you opening **Plugins** (via `/plugins` or the command palette) when this happened? If so, could you share:

- the exact launch command (especially whether you used `--server`), the action immediately before the crash, and whether it reproduces
- the output of `opencode2 plugin list --builtin` (please redact local paths if needed)
- the relevant `plugins` config entries, and whether a plugin had just failed or updated
- the server version from `opencode2 api get /api/health`
- any redacted log lines from around the crash

If you weren't in the Plugins dialog, which screen or dialog was active?

I reproduced the exact crash path: `0.0.0-beta-18371` opens `/plugins`, receives a newer server's package-plugin shape, and calls `localeCompare` on an undefined label.

That client expects package sources as `source.package`; the newer plugin API uses `source.target`. With two current-shape package entries, the old dialog crashes at the same bundled line. The current beta renders the same response normally.

Please also share the `/api/health` server version and launch command so we can confirm this was client/server version skew. In the meantime, updating the client and server to the same beta should avoid it.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #37935: Same root cause — broad deny overrides specific allow via last-match-wins (`findLast()`) semantics in the permission evaluator
- #39022: Plugin agent manifest permissions not overriding inherited default deny — very similar pattern of agent-specific allow losing to a broader deny
- #24335: Wildcard `*` deny overwriting more specific allow rules (same last-match-wins evaluation problem)

All three describe the same underlying issue: the permission evaluator uses last-match-wins ordering without considering rule specificity or scope (root vs. agent-level), so a broad wildcard deny can override a narrower explicit allow depending on rule registration order.
